description: Machine-readable capability manifest for the ESP32-2432S028R (CYD) board and every firmware project in this workspace. Loadable by any tool that can parse JSON.

usb_serial_chip.name: CH340
usb_serial_chip.com_port: assigned by Windows at plug time — seen as COM7 and COM8 on this machine
usb_serial_chip.resolve_with: esp32_port.py (auto-detect by PNP id); override with ESP32_PORT env var

network.ip_note: DHCP-assigned, changes between boots — re-check the serial log
network.outbound_only_note: device dials out; no inbound port forwarding needed (reverse relay pattern)

display.controller: ILI9341 (ST7789 on some variants — not auto-detected)
display.backlight_note: RST tied to EN; GPIO 27 on some variants instead of 21

touch.spi_bus: VSPI (SPI3) — separate from the display, this is the key CYD gotcha

speaker.amp: onboard class-D amp, fed from GPIO26 (analog input)
speaker.drive_method: ESP32 internal DAC through I2S: i2s_set_dac_mode(I2S_DAC_CHANNEL_LEFT_EN)

dac_mapping.I2S_DAC_CHANNEL_RIGHT_EN: DAC channel 0 -> GPIO25 (also the touch clock — do not use)

speaker.api_note: requires the legacy driver/i2s.h — the newer driver/i2s_std.h has no DAC mode
speaker.connector: P4, 2P 1.25 mm Molex PicoBlade, labelled SPEAK, on the back
speaker.speaker_note: speaker is optional; without one the board is silent but everything else still works

sd_card.spi_bus: VSPI (SPI3) — shares the bus with touch

microphone.note: no mic on board — voice input needs an external INMP441 I2S mic on free GPIOs

peripherals.free_gpios_note: GPIO 35 and 38 are input-only with no internal pull-ups; GPIO 21 is the backlight; 22 and 27 are broken out on the Molex connectors

connectors.P1: 4P Molex PicoBlade — VIN, IO1(TX), IO3(RX), GND
connectors.P3: 4P Molex PicoBlade — GND, IO35, IO22, IO21(backlight)

firmware_projects.title: SmartPLAY Live 放場通知器 (release-only)
firmware_projects.purpose: Standalone release alarm: the board tells you when evening court slots open up — one beep plus a full-screen card. Nothing else.
features: two independent paths, deduped so an event never beeps twice
PUSH: the board dials out to the VM (NAT-proof) and the VM pushes a release the moment the feed changes
POLL fallback: HTTPS GET changes-eve.json every 60 s
release detection: kind == 'chg' && new > old, or kind == 'new'
first poll is baseline-only — a reboot never false-alarms
one short quiet beep per release (1 kHz, 160 ms, raised-cosine envelope, I2S DAC left -> GPIO26)
full-screen alert card: sport, district, venue, time range, facility, old->new courts
green header bar + RGB LED green blink on alert
tap the touchscreen to dismiss; auto-dismiss after 120 s
status screen: last poll, next poll, feed version, releases seen, push link state
venue -> district resolved server-side (the board never downloads today.json)
CJK font subset generated from the live feed (323 glyphs / 10 KB)
NTP time (HKT) via configTime

push_protocol.transport: plain TCP, board dials out (no inbound ports)

serial_commands.p: audio probe — 880 Hz I2S-DAC-L(GPIO26), 1174 Hz I2S-DAC-R(GPIO25), 1567 Hz PWM(GPIO26)
serial_commands.l: print the releases seen since boot

verified.push_path: verified end-to-end locally by tools/cyd_push_test.py (handshake, version change, RELEASE delivered with venue + district)
verified.beep_audible: UNKNOWN — needs a human to confirm a speaker is plugged in

known_limitations: silent unless a speaker is connected to the SPEAK socket
push needs the daemon running on the VM and TCP 9000 open in the Oracle Cloud Security Group — currently closed, so the board runs on the 1-minute poll fallback
changes-eve.json has no district field; the VM fills it in from the venue->district map
the upstream LCSD mirror refreshes every 15 min — that dominates the end-to-end latency

firmware_projects.title: SOCKS5 proxy node + reverse relay
firmware_projects.status: source in repo — one command to restore
firmware_projects.purpose: Exits the residential IP through the board; also dials out to a VM so the VM can reach the board without port forwarding.
features: SOCKS5 with RFC 1929 username/password auth (slot=4)
listens on port 1080
4 concurrent sessions, 16 KB buffers per session
reverse relay: the board dials the VM on :9000 every 5 s with a 'CYD RELAY 1' handshake
hardening: pipelining leftover handling, per-ATYP length validation, blocking DNS/connect, EOF handling, 120 s idle timeout, WiFi reconnect with server.begin() re-run, WiFi.setSleep(false)
LED status: green ready, blue blink active, red no WiFi

firmware_projects.title: AI Math Tutor (touch chat toy)
firmware_projects.status: source in repo — verified on real hardware earlier
firmware_projects.purpose: Touch-driven AI tutor on the 2.8 inch panel with Chinese output.
features: state machine: WiFi list -> keyboard -> connecting -> chat -> settings -> model
layered on-screen keyboard (lower/upper/symbol, symbol layer +-*/=<>^_)
chat bubbles with word-wrap, drag-to-scroll, viewport clipping
NVS memory (namespace 'cydmath'): last 10 messages survive reboot, ~3900 B cap
OpenRouter free models with automatic fallback on 429, stops immediately on 401
max_tokens 320, last 6 messages as context, setInsecure() TLS
personas: Tutor / Short / Exam / Proof
RGB LED status, tone() beeps
CJK font: 16x16 1-bit, Big5 Level 1 + symbols, 5905 glyphs, ~196 KB flash
demo mode with no API key — playable immediately
known_limitations: keyboard is ASCII only — Chinese can only come from the AI or serial

firmware_projects.title: NEON SERPENT 3D wireless controller
firmware_projects.status: source in repo — verified by test/esp32-deep-test.mjs
firmware_projects.purpose: Touch game-pad that runs a WebSocket server; the game page connects as a client.
features: WebSocket server on port 8787
touch direction pad (FWD/BACK/LT/RT, Y+/Y-, PAUSE, AUTO) + BOOT button shortcuts
splash image (splash_data.h, RLE) + 'HELLO TEDDY!' banner + greeting melody on GPIO 26
RGB LED status: blue slow blink = setup, solid = linked
WiFi captive-portal setup (AP 'NEON-SERPENT-CYD' / 'serpent3d' / 192.168.4.1), credentials persisted in NVS, long-press BOOT 3 s to reset
protocol: board -> game join / autopilot / command / pause / resume; game -> board hello / state / response

scripts.purpose: resolve the CH340 COM port by PNP id; explicit arg > ESP32_PORT env > auto-detect
pytest suite for esp32_port (logic + live-hardware checks)
reset pulse + capture the ROM banner
serial monitor with a clean reset pulse
capture the SOCKS5 boot log and the WiFi/IP status
read serial without resetting, fire a SOCKS request, print device logs
automated CJK rendering test over serial
VM side: SOCKS reverse relay (pool :9000 / front :1080) AND the release push notifier (same port, 'CYD PUSH 1' greeting)
local end-to-end test of the push path — fake feed + fake board, asserts the RELEASE line arrives with venue + district
generate the 5905-glyph CJK font for the chat firmware
generate the feed-derived CJK subset for the smartplay firmware
verify every non-ASCII char used is covered by the font

standalone_onboard: WiFi station + TLS client (pull JSON feeds)
resistive touch input with its own SPI bus
audio output through the onboard amp (GPIO26, I2S DAC)
needs_extra_hardware: audio input — no microphone on board (INMP441 I2S mic on 3 free GPIOs)
onboard wake word — ESP-SR needs an ESP32-S3, not available on the classic ESP32
cleaner audio — the onboard amp is analog; an I2S DAC (MAX98357A) gives better TTS quality
not_possible_on_this_board: on-device ASR (Whisper-class needs ~100 MB and vector instructions)
true hands-free wake word on the classic ESP32
OTA with the current partition tables

future_voice_plan.recommended_mode: push-to-talk on the touchscreen, PC (or cloud) as the brain
future_voice_plan.why: the reverse relay already gives the needed always-reachable audio uplink/downlink; the ESP32 only needs I2S capture, PCM transport, screen UI and playback
phases: 0. quiet audio probe — is there actually a speaker on this board?
1. TTS playback — PC sends PCM, board plays it and shows the text
2. add an INMP441 mic — stream to the PC, run whisper, show the transcript
3. full loop + wake word (on the PC)
alternative_modes: B — hands-free with the wake word on the PC (mic always streaming)
C — on-device wake word (needs an ESP32-S3, different form factor)
D — voice output only (no mic; cheapest real voice win)
E — standalone, no PC (board calls cloud STT/TTS over its own WiFi)

docs.notes: this file is the machine-readable source of truth — regenerate it when the board or a firmware project changes

environment_notes: pio is not on PATH — use 'python -m platformio'
opening the CH340 port with DTR/RTS asserted resets the ESP32 — the helper scripts pulse RTS deliberately
COM3-COM6 on this machine are Bluetooth virtual serial ports (decoys) and must never be selected
the SOCKS proxy firmware is what is needed when the AWS VM must reach the house IP; smartplay is what the board is running now
the COM port number changes between replugs (COM7 -> COM8) — never hardcode it

test_esp32_port_py.note: the resolver was rewritten to use 'pnputil' (61 ms) instead of the WMI/CIM query (10.5 s)
